channel.title: Ceasefire Magazine – Bias and Credibility - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Ceasefire Magazine – Bias and Credibility (ceasefiremagazine.co.uk)

item.title: Elevation | Ceasefire Magazine
item.description: Over several months during lockdown, Dave Prescott became increasingly aware of an urge to see over the hedge of his back garden and across to the hills beyond. Naturally, he began to investigate the concept of an elevated chair.

item.title: The Girl in the Mirror: On Media Representations and Aesthetics of Shamima Begum | Ceasefire Magazine
item.description: Shamima Begum has become the repository of Britain's self-mythology around the ‘dangers’ of having so many of 'them’ amongst 'us', writes Fatima Rajina.

item.title: The Bigotry of Man: "Darwin's views on race were far from radical" | Ceasefire Magazine
item.description: It is 150 years since the publication of Darwin's The Descent of Man. Kezia Picard sat down with Samuel Grove, author of Retrieving Darwin’s Revolutionary Idea, to talk about the radical and reactionary implications of Darwin’s theory.

item.title: Profits before People: Britain's unjust housing system preys on asylum seekers | Ceasefire Magazine
item.description: The logic of asylum housing is simply an extension of the housing system in the UK more broadly. They are both underpinned by profiteering, deregulation, and racism, write Bogumila Hall and Ola Hall.

item.title: On the Nationality and Borders Bill and the UK Left | Ceasefire Magazine
item.description: The Nationality and Borders Bill, which goes to the House of Lords next week, presents a grave danger to Britain’s ethnic minorities. So why has there been so little opposition to it from the UK left? Asks Sam Asumadu.

item.title: For the Culture: Reflections on Black & Brown Activism | Ceasefire Magazine
item.description: Any black and brown activist knows activism carries an enormous personal cost, yet our campaigns continue to rely on the sacrifices of a few. The only way we can succeed is by working together, writes Samantha Asumadu.

item.title: Review | 'Come What May' by Ahmed Masoud | Ceasefire Magazine
item.description: Come What May, the latest novel by Palestinian author Ahmed Masoud, introduces us to the essential human story behind daily Palestinian issues and concerns, a story we rarely see in the press or on our TV screens, writes Amanda Huggins in her review.

item.title: The colonial clock and critical chaos at Kassel: Reflections on documenta 15 | Ceasefire Magazine
item.description: Art, aesthetics and racism are combined in a critical configuration that has transformed documenta fifteen into a significant political event, writes Iain Chambers.

item.title: Analysis | Echoes From the World Cup: Morocco and the Politics of Belonging | Ceasefire Magazine
item.description: The 2022 World Cup has showed that for Moroccans there is no contradictions in being African and Arab, in supporting the Palestinian cause and in embracing our Jewish communities, writes Maha Marouan.

item.title: Comment | Dispossession resistance is a natural law right of the Palestinian people | Ceasefire Magazine
item.description: The Palestinian struggle is very much one of the theft of land, and the choice of a people to not give up on that land and maintain their moral authority over it, writes Asim Qureshi.
